source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 13: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: TTFT is request arrival to first generated token, TPOT is the mean inter-token time after the first token (also report its distribution), throughput is completed output tokens/s and requests/s, and queueing is measured from arrival to service start. Treat these as measured quantities, not platform-independent guarantees. Hypothesis: at a fixed offered load and fixed prompt/output distribution, increasing concurrency improves throughput until prefill/decode contention or memory pressure causes queueing and P99 TTFT/latency to rise; separating prefill and decode scheduling will reduce that knee without violating the quality and error-rate guardrails. Build a replayable workload with fixed seed, arrival process, prompt-length and output-length distributions, concurrency, model/configuration, batch limits, and sampling settings. Compare a baseline scheduler with the proposed change using randomized or interleaved trials, identical warmup, and repeated runs. Discard or report warmup separately, then collect request timestamps, queue time, TTFT, per-token timestamps, TPOT percentiles, end-to-end latency percentiles including P99, completed token/request throughput, errors/timeouts, cancellation rate, GPU utilization, allocated/reserved/peak GPU memory, and request-level traces. Report units, sample counts, confidence intervals, and the exact workload mix; compute prefill and decode metrics separately because short prompts and long generations otherwise confound results. Check output correctness and reproducibility before comparing performance. Confounders include thermal or clock changes, background load, cache state, batching, host/network overhead, admission limits, OOM retries, and run-order effects. Roll back if correctness changes, error/timeout rate increases, memory approaches the tested safety limit, or P99 latency/SLOs regress beyond a predeclared threshold; canary first and retain an admission cap. Evidence required: controlled paired measurements on representative hardware and workload, trace-derived queue/prefill/decode attribution, and measured headroom rather than invented platform facts.
risks: TTFT, TPOT, queueing, and throughput definitions can vary and must be timestamped explicitly.
A mixed prompt/output distribution can hide prefill/decode regressions if not fixed and stratified.
Memory pressure, batching, clocks, background load, and run order can confound tail latency.
evidence_required: Run repeated controlled baseline and treatment trials with the exact workload distribution and warmup policy.
Validate request-level traces, prefill/decode attribution, GPU memory peaks, correctness, and error rates.
Predeclare SLO, memory, admission, and rollback thresholds and report uncertainty.
